patients.summary: Hodgkin survivor (2003 mantle radiation, splenectomy) with prostate cancer treated in 2020-21 and on leuprolide, who develops radiation-associated constrictive pericarditis treated by pericardiectomy in 2024, then metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer presenting as T8 cord compression in 2025 with a local recurrence in 2026. Chart with gaps: some oncology and urology letters never arrive.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 56 y/o man transferring care.

He is here mostly to get set up. Feels well. Works as a logistics coordinator for a distributor, a lot of time at a desk and on the phone, some walking the warehouse floor. No chest pain, no breathing trouble with his usual activity, no swelling. Sleeps fine.

Oncology history as he tells it and as his paperwork shows: Hodgkin lymphoma stage II in 2003, staged with a laparotomy and splenectomy, treated with mantle field radiation, no recurrence since. Prostate adenocarcinoma Gleason 3+4 found in 2020; radical retropubic prostatectomy with pelvic node dissection in October 2020, then adjuvant external beam radiation in early 2021 with leuprolide, which urology has kept going. He gets the 7.5 mg injection there every 28 days and they check his PSA. Bone density at his old office earlier this year showed osteopenia, blamed on the hormone therapy; takes calcium with D twice a day.
Other: hypertension and high cholesterol for several years. Right hip scope around 2013.

Meds: amlodipine 5 daily, atorvastatin 20 daily, aspirin 81 daily, calcium carbonate 600 / D3 400 twice daily, leuprolide 7.5 mg IM q28 days (urology).
Allergies: penicillin (rash); shellfish (anaphylaxis, had a reaction years ago at a restaurant). Has never had an epinephrine pen.
Family: father prostate cancer at 72, now deceased; mother breast cancer at 68; maternal grandfather coronary disease.
Social: married. Former smoker, about 20 pack-years, stopped in 2017. A drink or two on weekends. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: BP and vitals per flowsheet. Well appearing. Healed midline and lower abdominal scars. Neck supple, no thyromegaly or nodes. Heart regular, no murmur or rub. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Legs without edema. Gait normal.

Assessment and plan:
1. HTN, controlled on amlodipine 5. Continue.
2. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 20. Fasting lipids today.
3. Prostate cancer on ADT, followed by urology. Asked him to have their letters copied to us.
4. Hodgkin survivor after mantle radiation and splenectomy. TSH today and yearly. Asplenic: PCV20 given today; meningococcal vaccines at next visit once old records confirm what he had in 2003.
5. Osteopenia on ADT: continue calcium/D; repeat DXA in about two years.
6. Shellfish anaphylaxis: epinephrine auto-injector prescribed, showed him how to use the trainer.
7. Lung screening: qualifies by pack-years and quit date. Low-dose CT ordered.
8. Hep C and HIV screening today. CMP, CBC, vitamin D.
Records release already sent. Follow-up in about 5 months.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Nadeau, your bloodwork from Tuesday looks good. Kidney and liver tests, blood counts and thyroid are normal, vitamin D is fine on what you take, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. LDL cholesterol is about 100 on atorvastatin, which is acceptable; we'll keep the current dose. The lung CT scheduling desk should call you this week.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry of the lumbar spine (L1-L4) and left hip. Indication: androgen deprivation therapy. Lumbar spine L1-L4 T-score -1.4. Left femoral neck T-score -1.8. Left total hip T-score -1.2. No prior study for comparison.
reports.conclusion: Osteopenia. Lowest T-score -1.8 at the left femoral neck.

84 pages received by fax from prior primary care office, covering 2016 to 2022. Scanned. Items abstracted for PCP review:
- DXA 2/10/2022: osteopenia, femoral neck T -1.8, spine -1.4.
- Screening colonoscopy 4/23/2019: normal to the cecum, good prep, next in 10 years.
- Immunizations: pneumococcal polysaccharide and Hib in February 2003 before splenectomy; a meningococcal vaccine listed the same month, product not named. Flu shots most years.
- Problem list matches what patient reported. BP log mostly 120s-130s/70s-80s on amlodipine.
PCP reviewed 6/29: will give MenACWY and start MenB in the fall.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast. Comparison: none.
Lungs: no pulmonary nodules. No consolidation.
Pleura: no effusion.
Heart and mediastinum: heart size normal. Scattered pericardial calcification, consistent with prior radiation. No pericardial effusion. No lymphadenopathy. Coronary calcification not seen.
Upper abdomen: surgically absent spleen.
Bones: no suspicious lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

Outside urology group. Visit date 08/02/2022.
Re: Howard Nadeau, DOB 12/08/1965.

Thank you for taking over his primary care. He is now about 21 months past radical retropubic prostatectomy with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy for Gleason 3+4 adenocarcinoma, followed by adjuvant external beam radiation with concurrent androgen deprivation. He continues leuprolide 7.5 mg IM every 28 days in our office. Continent. No bone pain.
Allergies: penicillin (rash), shellfish (anaphylaxis).
PSA today: <0.1 ng/mL, undetectable.
Plan: continue leuprolide; PSA every 6 to 8 months; calcium and vitamin D for bone health.
Outside urology

Follow-up. Busy season at work, otherwise fine. Takes amlodipine and atorvastatin every morning, no side effects he notices. Home BP readings 120s/70s. Urology letter from August reviewed: PSA undetectable, leuprolide continues.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.

- Hypertension at goal; no change.
- Lipids acceptable on atorvastatin 20.
- Asplenia vaccines: MenACWY and first MenB today. Shingrix #1 today too, he was fine with three shots. Second Shingrix and MenB in 2 months, nurse visit.
- Physical in spring.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam.

Generally well. Only new thing: for a few weeks his ankles look a bit puffy by evening, gone by morning. No shortness of breath he's noticed, no chest symptoms, sleeping flat. Urology in March: PSA still undetectable.
Meds unchanged. Allergies: PCN, shellfish (has his epi pen).
No tobacco. PHQ-9 1.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Alert, comfortable. HEENT unremarkable. Neck: no thyromegaly. Heart regular, normal S1 S2, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Trace ankle edema bilaterally, nonpitting. Skin warm. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
1. Ankle swelling, mild, dependent. Most likely amlodipine. He doesn't want to change a pill that's been working; fine to watch, elevate legs, let me know if it climbs.
2. HTN at goal.
3. Lipids, CMP, CBC, TSH today.
4. Annual low-dose CT due in July, ordered.
5. Colonoscopy current to 2029. Vaccines up to date except flu/COVID in the fall.
See in 6 months.

documents.body: Howard, labs from your physical are all in the normal or expected range: kidneys, liver, blood counts, thyroid. Cholesterol is about the same as last year. Nothing to change. The CT scheduler will reach out about July.

orders.reason: progressive edema, increasing abdominal girth and exertional dyspnea; history of mantle radiation

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in because his belt doesn't close anymore. Thinking back, his belly has been growing and his legs swelling since around April, slowly. Now winded on the stairs at work and walking the loading dock, which is new. No chest pain, no palpitations, no fainting. Not short of breath at rest. Still on amlodipine 5, atorvastatin, aspirin, calcium/D, leuprolide.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet; weight up about 3 kg since May. Neck veins look full sitting up. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen distended, soft, nontender. Pitting edema of both legs to mid-shin.

A/P
Six months of edema, abdominal distension and exertional dyspnea. This is more than amlodipine. With mantle radiation in 2003 I am concerned about a cardiac cause: radiation heart disease, pericardial or myocardial. Urgent cardiology referral today; their office can see him within a few weeks and will do echo there. Low salt in the meantime. To call or go to the ED if breathing worsens or chest pain.

documents.body: Cardiology office called back: first available urgent new patient slot Monday 10/9, 9:00, with echo the same morning. Patient notified and agreed. Referral and last two notes faxed over.

medications.reason: constrictive pericarditis with edema and ascites

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Curvilinear calcification along the pericardium, best seen on the lateral view. Cardiac silhouette normal in size. Lungs clear. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax.

Technically adequate study. Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall thickness and normal systolic function. Right ventricle normal in size and function. The pericardium is thickened and bright. Mitral inflow and tissue Doppler show impaired diastolic filling. No pericardial effusion. Valves without significant stenosis or regurgitation.
reports.conclusion: Thickened pericardium with normal systolic function and impaired diastolic filling, concerning for constrictive physiology.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Consultation 10/09/2023.
Referring: primary care.
Patient: Howard Nadeau, 57 years old.

Reason: half a year of rising abdominal girth, leg swelling and exertional breathlessness.

HPI: Mr. Nadeau describes six months of slowly worsening swelling of the abdomen and legs and breathlessness with exertion. He has had no chest pain, palpitations or syncope.

Background: stage II Hodgkin lymphoma in 2003 with mantle field radiation and staging splenectomy, in remission. Prostate adenocarcinoma Gleason 3+4, radical prostatectomy 2020 then adjuvant external beam radiation, on leuprolide. Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, osteopenia on ADT. Right hip arthroscopy.
Medications: leuprolide 7.5 mg IM every 28 days; amlodipine 5 mg daily; atorvastatin 20 mg daily; calcium carbonate/vitamin D3 600 mg/400 IU twice daily; aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: penicillin (rash), shellfish (anaphylaxis).
Family: father prostate cancer, mother breast cancer, maternal grandfather coronary disease.
Social: former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 2017. Alcohol 1 to 2 drinks weekly. Logistics coordinator.

Exam: BP 115/75, HR 88, RR 18. Jugular venous pressure elevated. A pericardial knock is audible in early diastole. Abdomen distended with a fluid wave. Liver edge palpable 3 cm below the right costal margin. Pitting edema 2+ in both legs to the knees. Lungs clear.

Data: Hgb 13.2, WBC 7.8, platelets 235, creatinine 1.1, albumin 3.5, ALT 45, AST 50, total bilirubin 1.2, BNP 150.
Chest x-ray: pericardial calcifications.
Echo: thickened pericardium, normal systolic function, impaired diastolic filling.

Impression: constrictive pericarditis, almost certainly a late effect of mantle radiation, with right-sided congestion (ascites, hepatic congestion, edema). The modest BNP fits constriction rather than myocardial failure.

Plan:
1. Start furosemide 40 mg every morning; BMP in one week (asked PCP to draw).
2. Cardiac MRI for pericardial thickness and ventricular interdependence.
3. Right and left heart catheterization to confirm constrictive hemodynamics and look at the coronaries before any surgery.
4. If confirmed, refer for pericardiectomy.
5. Continue other medications.
Thank you for the referral.
Outside cardiology

documents.title: Water pill timing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Heart doctor started me on furosemide. I'm at work by 7 and in and out of the bathroom all morning. Can I take it at lunch instead? Also they said you'd do a blood test next week.

documents.title: RE: Water pill timing
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Yes, taking it at lunch is fine, just not later than mid-afternoon or you'll be up at night. The lab order is in for Tuesday 10/17, any time after 7:30. Keep weighing yourself in the morning and write it down for cardiology.

documents.title: BMP result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Electrolytes and creatinine fine one week into furosemide. Copied to cardiology.

documents.title: Cardiac MRI report (outside)
documents.author: radiology
documents.body:
Outside imaging center. Cardiac MRI with and without gadolinium, 10/30/2023.
Indication: suspected constrictive pericarditis after mantle radiation.
Findings: Pericardium diffusely thickened, up to 6 mm over the right ventricle. Septal bounce on cine imaging with exaggerated septal shift on free-breathing sequences, consistent with ventricular interdependence. LV normal in size, LVEF 58%. RV normal in size and function. No myocardial late gadolinium enhancement. Small ascites in the visualized upper abdomen. No pericardial effusion.
Impression: Findings consistent with constrictive pericarditis. Normal biventricular systolic function, LVEF 58%.

documents.title: Cardiac catheterization report (outside)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiac catheterization laboratory. Date 11/20/2023.
Procedure: right and left heart catheterization with coronary angiography, right radial and right femoral venous access. Allergies reviewed: penicillin, shellfish (anaphylaxis); no iodinated contrast reaction history; premedication not required.
Hemodynamics: RA 18 mmHg. RV end-diastolic 19 mmHg with dip-and-plateau waveform. PCWP 19 mmHg. LVEDP 20 mmHg. Near-equalization of diastolic pressures. Simultaneous LV/RV tracings show discordant respiratory variation of systolic pressures.
Coronaries: no obstructive coronary artery disease.
Conclusion: hemodynamics diagnostic of constrictive pericarditis. No obstructive CAD. Refer to cardiac surgery for pericardiectomy.
No complications; discharged same day.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, he's in his car on lunch break, verified DOB.

Wanted to talk through the cardiac surgery recommendation. Reviewed with him: MRI 10/30 shows thickened pericardium 6 mm and normal pumping, LVEF 58%; cath 11/20 confirmed constrictive physiology and no blockages. Surgeon visit done; pericardiectomy planned for 1/16. On furosemide 40, swelling down and belt fits again, still winded on stairs. Weight 87-88 kg at home.

We talked about why surgery is offered, that recovery after radiation-related constriction can be slower, and what the first weeks look like. He feels clear about going ahead.

Plan: hold aspirin per surgeon's instructions before surgery. Keep taking amlodipine and atorvastatin. Urology aware; leuprolide timing coordinated with them. I'll see him after discharge.
